root_cause.text: In the nested virtualization code when FEAT_XNX is not present, the code incorrectly uses FIELD_PREP() on an already-extracted 2-bit XN value to mask off XN[0], but FIELD_PREP shifts the mask to the original descriptor bitfield position, causing both XN bits to be cleared and thus unconditionally granting execute permissions.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `xn &= FIELD_PREP(KVM_PTE_LEAF_ATTR_HI_S2_XN, 0b10);` to `xn &= 0b10;` in both `kvm_s2_trans_exec_el0` and `kvm_s2_trans_exec_el1`. The CVE description states that "XN has already been extracted from its bitfield position so using FIELD_PREP() on the mask that clears XN[0] is completely broken, having the effect of unconditionally granting execute permissions".

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix incorrect masking of the XN attribute field by replacing FIELD_PREP with a direct bitmask, ensuring proper behavior when XNX is not supported.
intent_record.what: Replaced a call to FIELD_PREP(KVM_PTE_LEAF_ATTR_HI_S2_XN, 0b10) with the literal constant 0b10 in the expression that masks the variable xn.
intent_record.how: When kvm_has_xnx returns false, the code now applies a simple bitwise AND with 0b10 to the xn field value (which is already in the low bits), instead of applying a shifted mask that may not align with xn's bit positions. This corrects the masking logic so that only the second bit (bit 1) is retained.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix incorrect masking of the XN bit when XNX is absent by using a direct bitmask instead of a shifted field prep.
intent_record.what: In the conditional block when XNX is not supported, the mask applied to xn was changed from `FIELD_PREP(KVM_PTE_LEAF_ATTR_HI_S2_XN, 0b10)` to `0b10`.
intent_record.how: Previously, the code used a macro that shifts the value into the field's bit positions, but since xn is already the extracted field value (right-aligned), this shifted mask would not align correctly, leading to incorrect behavior (likely always zeroing the relevant bit). The new code directly uses the binary mask 0b10, which correctly selects the high bit of the two-bit xn field.

commit d93febe2ed2e0491af9d47f0ee6d4b01918877f4
Author: Oliver Upton <oupton@kernel.org>
Date:   Mon Nov 24 11:01:45 2025 -0800

    KVM: arm64: nv: Forward FEAT_XNX permissions to the shadow stage-2
    
    Add support for FEAT_XNX to shadow stage-2 MMUs, being careful to only
    evaluate XN[0] when the feature is actually exposed to the VM.
    Restructure the layering of permissions in the fault handler to assume
    pX and uX then restricting based on the guest's stage-2 afterwards.
bic_trace_step.reason: The functions kvm_s2_trans_exec_el0 and kvm_s2_trans_exec_el1 extract the 2-bit XN value using FIELD_GET and then apply 'xn &= FIELD_PREP(KVM_PTE_LEAF_ATTR_HI_S2_XN, 0b10);' when FEAT_XNX is not present. This is the exact bug described in the root cause: FIELD_PREP shifts the value to the original descriptor bit positions, but xn is already a 2-bit integer, so the AND operation clears both XN bits instead of just XN[0], unconditionally granting execute permissions.
